cards.canonical_statement: If A is a linear map and domain of A is finite-dimensional, rank(A) is at most dimension(domain(A)).

cards.proof_strategy: Apply the finite-dimensional range bound for a linear map.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a field and finite-dimensional domain V for the linear map A.
translate: Read rank(A) as the dimension of range(A).
apply_theorem: Apply the range-dimension bound for linear maps.
conclude: The rank cannot exceed dimension(V).
cards.lean_witness: example {K V W : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (A : V →ₗ[K] W) : Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range A) ≤ Module.finrank K V := LinearMap.finrank_range_le A

cards.canonical_statement: If A is a linear map and domain of A is finite-dimensional, nullity(A) is at most dimension(domain(A)).

cards.proof_strategy: Combine rank-nullity with nonnegativity of the rank.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix A with finite-dimensional domain V.
apply_theorem: Write rank(A) + nullity(A) = dimension(V).
derive: Use nonnegativity of rank(A).
conclude: Nullity(A) is bounded by dimension(V).
cards.lean_witness:
example {K V W : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (A : V →ₗ[K] W) : Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker A) ≤ Module.finrank K V := by
  have h := LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker A
  omega

cards.canonical_statement: For a linear map A with finite-dimensional domain, rank(A) < dimension(domain(A)) entails 0 < nullity(A).

cards.proof_strategy: Use rank-nullity to turn a strict rank deficit into a positive kernel dimension.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix A and assume its rank is strictly below the domain dimension.
apply_theorem: Expand dimension(V) using rank-nullity.
derive: Rewrite the strict inequality as a positive natural-number remainder.
interpret: Identify that remainder with nullity(A).
conclude: The kernel has positive dimension.
cards.lean_witness:
example {K V W : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (A : V →ₗ[K] W) (hdeficit : Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range A) < Module.finrank K V) : 0 < Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker A) := by
  have h := LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker A
  omega

cards.canonical_statement: For a linear map A with finite-dimensional domain, rank(A) = dimension(domain(A)) entails nullity(A) = 0.

cards.proof_strategy: Substitute the full-rank hypothesis into rank-nullity and cancel the common term.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix A and assume that its rank equals the domain dimension.
apply_theorem: Write rank(A) + nullity(A) = dimension(V).
substitute: Replace rank(A) by dimension(V).
derive: Cancel the equal dimension terms in the natural-number equality.
conclude: Nullity(A) is zero.

example {K V W : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (A : V →ₗ[K] W) (hfull : Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range A) = Module.finrank K V) : Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker A) = 0 := by
  have h := LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker A
  omega

cards.proof_strategy: Use rank-nullity with the maximal-nullity hypothesis.

cards.canonical_statement: If a is real, then the function x ↦ (x-a)/(x^2-(2*a*x)+a^2+1) is continuous on the real line.

cards.proof_strategy: Prove the quadratic denominator is strictly positive, then apply quotient continuity.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a real parameter a and set q(x)=x²-2ax+a²+1.
rewrite: Complete the square to obtain q(x)=(x-a)²+1.
derive: Use square nonnegativity to prove q(x)>0 for every real x.
apply_theorem: The numerator and denominator are polynomial functions, hence continuous.
conclude: Apply the quotient-continuity theorem using q(x)≠0.
cards.lean_witness:
example (a : ℝ) : Continuous (fun x : ℝ => (x - a) / (x^2 - 2*a*x + a^2 + 1)) := by
  apply Continuous.div
  · fun_prop
  · fun_prop
  · intro x
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x - a)]

cards.proof_strategy: Combine continuity of absolute value with a positive quadratic denominator.
sketch_steps: setup: Let q(x)=x²+1.
derive: Since x²≥0, q(x)>0 for all real x.
apply_theorem: Absolute value and q are continuous functions.
apply_theorem: Use quotient continuity with the nonvanishing denominator.
conclude: The displayed rational absolute-value function is continuous everywhere.

  · fun_prop

cards.proof_strategy: Use continuity of a polynomial to obtain its punctured-neighborhood limit.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix a real point a.
identify: The displayed expression is a polynomial in x.
apply_theorem: Polynomials are continuous at a.
derive: Continuity gives convergence on ordinary neighborhoods.
restrict: Pass to the punctured neighborhood at a.
conclude: Evaluate the polynomial at a to obtain the claimed limit.
cards.lean_witness:
example (a : ℝ) : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => x^2 + 3*x - 1) (nhdsWithin a ({a} : Set ℝ)ᶜ) (nhds (a^2 + 3*a - 1)) := by
  have h : ContinuousAt (fun x : ℝ => x^2 + 3*x - 1) a := by fun_prop
  exact h.tendsto.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds

cards.canonical_statement: The limit of x ↦ (x^2-4)/(x-2) at 2 is 4.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMA><OMS cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" cd="pals1" name="has_limit_at"/><OMBIND><OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMI>4</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMBIND><OMI>2</OMI><OMI>4</OMI></OMA></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Factor the numerator away from the excluded point, then take the limit of the simplified affine function.
sketch_steps: setup: Work in the punctured neighborhood of 2, where x-2 is nonzero.
factor: Rewrite x²-4 as (x-2)(x+2).
simplify: Cancel x-2 on the punctured neighborhood to get x+2.
apply_theorem: The affine function x↦x+2 is continuous at 2.
evaluate: Its value at 2 is 4.
conclude: Transfer the limit through the eventual equality.
cards.lean_witness:
example : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (x^2 - 4) / (x - 2)) (nhdsWithin (2 : ℝ) ({(2 : ℝ)} : Set ℝ)ᶜ) (nhds 4) := by
  have hEq : (fun x : ℝ => (x^2 - 4) / (x - 2)) =ᶠ[nhdsWithin (2 : ℝ) ({(2 : ℝ)} : Set ℝ)ᶜ] fun x => x + 2 := by
    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with x hx
    simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    have hx0 : x - 2 ≠ 0 := by
      intro hzero
      apply hx
      linarith
    field_simp [hx0]
    ring
  have h : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => x + 2) (nhdsWithin (2 : ℝ) ({(2 : ℝ)} : Set ℝ)ᶜ) (nhds 4) := by
    have hcont : ContinuousAt (fun x : ℝ => x + 2) (2 : ℝ) := by fun_prop
    have hfilter : nhdsWithin (2 : ℝ) ({(2 : ℝ)} : Set ℝ)ᶜ ≤ nhds (2 : ℝ) := nhdsWithin_le_nhds
    convert hcont.tendsto.mono_left hfilter using 1 <;> norm_num
  exact h.congr' hEq.symm

cards.canonical_statement: For sets A, B, C, (A ∪ B) × C = (A × C) ∪ (B × C).

cards.proof_strategy: Expand membership of an ordered pair and distribute the left disjunction.
sketch_steps: setup: Take an arbitrary ordered pair (x,y).
expand: Interpret membership in (A∪B)×C componentwise.
split: Separate the cases x∈A and x∈B.
reassemble: Recognize membership in (A×C)∪(B×C).
conclude: Extensionality proves the set equality.
cards.lean_witness:
example {α β : Type*} (A B : Set α) (C : Set β) : (A ∪ B) ×ˢ C = (A ×ˢ C) ∪ (B ×ˢ C) := by
  ext p
  simp [and_or_left]

sketch_steps: setup: Take an arbitrary ordered pair (x,y).

cards.proof_strategy: Use pair membership to move conjunctions between factors and products.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix an ordered pair (x,y).
expand: Write membership in (A∩B)×C as x∈A, x∈B, y∈C.
